issues.title: [BUG] marketplace.json omits description/version for local virtual-subdirectory packages (only remote packages are enriched)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

For a monorepo that is **its own marketplace** and references its packages by **local virtual-subdirectory** source (`source: ./packages/<name>`), `apm pack` produces a `marketplace.json` whose plugin entries have **no `description` and no `version`** — even though every package's own `apm.yml` declares both. `apm marketplace browse <name>` therefore renders `--` in the **Description** and **Version** columns for every plugin.

The metadata enrichment that fills these fields runs for **remote** packages only: the builder fetches `description`/`version` from a package's `apm.yml` over the network, but for a local-path package it never reads the `apm.yml` sitting on disk next to the manifest. The Claude output mapper has no local fallback, so unless the curator **duplicates** `description`/`version` onto each marketplace entry by hand, local entries are emitted with only `name`/`source`/`tags`. Note the asymmetry: `tags` declared on the entry pass through fine, so the manifest is valid — only the package-owned `description`/`version` are silently lost.

Verified against apm-cli 0.19.0 by reading the source and with live `apm pack` runs.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. A monorepo marketplace whose entries reference packages by local subpath, with the per-package metadata owned by each package's manifest:

   ```yaml
   # apm.yml (repo root)
   marketplace:
     owner: { name: tester, url: https://github.com/tester }
     outputs: { claude: {} }
     packages:
       - name: foo
         source: ./packages/foo
         tags: [demo]
   ```

   ```yaml
   # packages/foo/apm.yml
   name: foo
   version: 1.2.3
   description: A local foo package with real metadata.
   type: skill
   target: all
   ```

2. Run `apm pack --offline`.
3. Inspect `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.

Observed — `description` and `version` are dropped, even though `packages/foo/apm.yml` declares them:

```json
{
  "name": "foo",
  "tags": ["demo"],
  "source": "./packages/foo"
}
```

Duplicating the same fields onto the marketplace **entry** makes them appear, which confirms the serialization path itself works — only the local-source-of-truth read is missing:

```yaml
    - name: foo
      source: ./packages/foo
      tags: [demo]
      description: A local foo package with real metadata.
      version: 1.2.3
```

```json
{
  "name": "foo",
  "description": "A local foo package with real metadata.",
  "version": "1.2.3",
  "tags": ["demo"],
  "source": "./packages/foo"
}
```

A real-world instance: a 96-package monorepo marketplace, all local subpath sources, every package `apm.yml` carrying `version` + `description` → all 96 browse entries show empty Description/Version.

**Expected behavior**

For a local-path (virtual-subdirectory) package, the builder should read `<source>/apm.yml` from disk and inherit `description`/`version` (and the other Anthropic pass-through metadata) the same way it fetches them from the remote `apm.yml` for remote packages — a local-filesystem mirror of the existing remote-metadata fetch. Curator-supplied values on the marketplace entry should still take precedence. This matches the intent already stated in the code (`_prefetch_metadata` documents that *"Local-path packages are skipped (they carry their own metadata)"*) — but that local metadata is never actually read, so the field ends up empty instead of inherited.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux (WSL2)
 - Python Version: 3.14
 - APM Version: 0.19.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a

**Logs**

`apm marketplace browse` against such a marketplace (Description / Version empty for every plugin):

```
                         Plugins in 'example-marketplace'
┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ Plugin                       ┃ Description ┃ Version ┃ Install               ┃
┡━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ foo                          │ --          │   --    │ foo@example-marketpl… │
└──────────────────────────────┴─────────────┴─────────┴───────────────────────┘
```

`apm pack --offline` reports success while emitting the metadata-less entries:

```
[*] Built marketplace.json [claude] (1 package(s)) -> .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
```

**Additional context**

Source-level root cause (apm-cli 0.19.0):

1. `marketplace/builder.py` (`_resolve_entry`) resolves a local entry with `source_repo=""` (the `if entry.is_local:` branch). The `source_repo` field is what later marks a package as "remote".

2. `marketplace/builder.py` (`_prefetch_metadata`) builds the `{name: {description, version}}` map but first filters to remote entries only:
   ```python
   # Local-path packages are skipped (they carry their own metadata).
   remote = [pkg for pkg in resolved if pkg.source_repo]
   ```
   Because local packages have `source_repo == ""`, they are excluded from enrichment entirely. The comment asserts local packages "carry their own metadata", but nothing downstream reads it.

3. `marketplace/builder.py` (`_fetch_remote_metadata`) is documented as *"fetch `description` and `version` from the package's **remote** `apm.yml`"* and reaches over the network (GitHub host / token aware). There is no local-filesystem counterpart that reads `<source>/apm.yml`.

4. `marketplace/output_mappers.py` (`ClaudeMarketplaceMapper`, `uses_remote_metadata = True`) emits `description`/`version` differently for local vs remote:
   ```python
   if is_local:
       if entry.description:
           plugin["description"] = entry.description
       if entry.version:
           plugin["version"] = entry.version
   else:
       meta = remote_metadata.get(pkg.name, {})
       ...
       elif meta.get("description"):
           plugin["description"] = meta["description"]
       ...
       elif meta.get("version"):
           plugin["version"] = meta["version"]
   ```
   The remote branch falls back to the fetched `remote_metadata`; the local branch only emits curator-supplied `entry.description`/`entry.version` and has **no fallback** to the package's on-disk `apm.yml`. (The `CodexMarketplaceMapper` is unaffected — that format carries `category`, not `description`/`version`.)

Net: for a monorepo-as-marketplace using local subpath sources, every plugin's `apm.yml` (with `version` + `description`) is on disk right beside its manifest, but the builder never reads it, so the generated `marketplace.json` omits both fields.

Workaround in use: a CI step discovers every `packages/*/apm.yml` and writes `description`/`version` onto each marketplace entry in the root `apm.yml` before `apm pack`, so the fields are present on the entry by the time the Claude mapper runs.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-11
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-11
**APM Version**: 0.19.0 (cb9fb93)
**Commands Inspected**: 27

All commands were run directly via the installed `apm` CLI. Every finding below is backed by exact command output.

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

None found.

---

### Medium Severity

#### 1. `apm mcp install --help` surfaces forwarded options as unstructured epilog text

- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: The formal `Options:` block shows only `--help`. The options that are actually accepted (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `--dev`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--verbose`, `--no-policy`) appear only as free-form text in an epilog paragraph. Users who rely on `--help` to discover options cannot see their types, defaults, or descriptions. The options do work at runtime (they are forwarded to `apm install --mcp`), but they are undiscoverable through the standard help interface.
- **Evidence**:
```
$ apm mcp install --help
Usage: apm mcp install [OPTIONS] NAME

  Add an MCP server to apm.yml. Alias for 'apm install --mcp'.

  Examples:
    apm mcp install fetch -- npx -y `@modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch`
    apm mcp install api --transport http --url (example.com/redacted)

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

  Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
  [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
  transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
  KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
  --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
  run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
```
- **Suggested Fix**: Declare the forwarded options explicitly as Click parameters on `apm mcp install` (or use a shared option group / decorator), so they appear as properly formatted entries in the `Options:` block with their types and descriptions.

---

#### 2. `apm uninstall` lacks `-y/--yes` for non-interactive / CI use

- **Command**: `apm uninstall`
- **Problem**: `apm uninstall` removes packages, their deployed files, and `apm.yml` entries -- a destructive, irreversible operation -- yet it exposes no `--yes` flag to skip a confirmation prompt in CI or scripting contexts. By contrast, `apm update` (`-y, --yes`) and `apm deps clean` (`-y, --yes`) both have this flag. Without `--yes`, scripts that need to remove a package non-interactively must pipe `y` or use workarounds.
- **Evidence**:
```
$ apm uninstall --help
Usage: apm uninstall [OPTIONS] PACKAGES...

  Remove APM packages, their integrated files, and apm.yml entries

Options:
  --dry-run      Show what would be removed without removing
  -v, --verbose  Show detailed removal information
  -g, --global   Remove from user scope (~/.apm/) instead of the current project
  --help         Show this message and exit.
```
Compare `apm update --help`:
```
  -y, --yes   Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)
```
And `apm deps clean --help`:
```
  -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt
```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-y, --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)` to `apm uninstall`.

---

#### 3. Inconsistent description wording between `apm update` and `apm deps update`

- **Commands**: `apm update`, `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: Both commands perform the same conceptual operation (refresh git refs and reinstall packages), but their one-line descriptions use different verbs and phrasing. `apm update` uses "Refresh", `apm deps update` uses "Update". Since `apm deps update` is deprecated in favor of `apm update`, clarifying the deprecation in the `apm deps update` one-liner would also help users understand the relationship.
- **Evidence**:
```
$ apm update --help
  Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs

$ apm deps update --help
  Update APM dependencies to latest refs
```
- **Suggested Fix**: Update `apm deps update`'s one-liner to something like `"[Deprecated: use 'apm update'] Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs"`, making the deprecation and canonical replacement explicit at the summary level.

---

### Low Severity

#### 4. Inconsistent trailing periods in top-level command descriptions

- **Commands**: `pack`, `publish`, `self-update`, `targets`, `unpack`
- **Problem**: Five top-level command descriptions in `apm --help` end with a trailing period; the remaining ~25 commands do not. This is a style inconsistency.
- **Evidence** (from `apm --help`, commands whose descriptions end with a period):
```
  pack          Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.
  publish       Publish a package to a registry.
  self-update   Update the APM CLI binary itself to the latest version.
  targets       Show resolved targets for the current project.
  unpack        [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.
```
Versus (no trailing period -- representative):
```
  compile       Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files
  config        Configure APM CLI
  deps          Manage APM package dependencies
  init          Initialize a new APM project
  mcp           Discover, inspect, and install MCP servers
  update        Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs
```
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove trailing periods from `pack`, `publish`, `self-update`, `targets`, and `unpack` descriptions to match the majority convention.

---

#### 5. `apm compile --no-dedup / --no-force-instructions` flag naming is a double-negative

- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: The flag that enables inclusion of the instructions section in `CLAUDE.md` is named `--no-dedup` as its primary form. The action is positive ("Include the instructions section") but the primary flag name starts with `--no-`. The alias `--force-instructions` (mentioned only in the description text) is far more intuitive but is secondary. Users reading the help must mentally decode "no-dedup means include instructions" rather than immediately understanding the intent.
- **Evidence**:
```
$ apm compile --help
  --no-dedup / --no-force-instructions
                                  Include the instructions section in
                                  CLAUDE.md even when .claude/rules/ is
                                  already populated. Overrides the default
                                  deduplication that normally omits the
                                  section to avoid duplicate context in Claude
                                  Code. Affects the Claude target only. Alias:
                                  --force-instructions.
```
- **Suggested Fix**: Make `--force-instructions` the primary flag name (shown first in the option declaration) and keep `--no-dedup` as the backward-compatible alias. Update the help description to drop the "Alias:" note.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks:

- **Error handling**: All invalid-argument scenarios tested (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no arg, `apm config set` with no args) produced clean, actionable error messages with no tracebacks.
- **`-h / --help`**: Works on every command and subcommand inspected.
- **`apm init`**: Consistent flags; deprecation notices for `--plugin` and `--marketplace` are clear.
- **`apm install`**: Comprehensive option set, detailed descriptions, consistent with docs.
- **`apm update`**: Consistent with docs; has `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`, `-g`.
- **`apm compile`**: Full option set, well-described (aside from finding #5 above).
- **`apm run`**: Clean, minimal, consistent with docs.
- **`apm deps list/tree/info/clean`**: Internally consistent within the subset; docs match CLI.
- **`apm mcp search/show/list`**: Consistent flags and descriptions; default limits match docs (search: 10, list: 20).
- **`apm config get/set/unset`**: Consistent with docs; docs accurately describe the absence of a `list` subcommand.
- **`apm runtime setup/list/status/remove`**: All subcommands exist as documented; `apm runtime remove` correctly exposes `-y, --yes`.
- **Documentation cross-reference**: All commands listed in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` exist in the actual CLI. No phantom commands or missing pages detected.

issues.title: Epic: Strengthen install-time supply-chain integrity and policy clarity
issues.body:
## Summary
APM's role is the install-and-integrity layer for agent primitives (skills, agents, instructions, MCP server configs): resolve, pin, hash, lock, verify, and record what gets installed. Agent harnesses own runtime governance -- what a running agent may do once installed. This epic groups work that makes that separation explicit and deepens APM's install-time integrity guarantees.

## Why now
Two recurring sources of confusion and risk:
1. Users are unsure what `apm-policy.yml` governs. Because it exposes allow/deny lists, it can read like a generic permission system, when its actual job is the install contract: which sources are trusted, which versions are installed, and whether artifacts are verified.
2. Agent primitives increasingly reach a developer machine through multiple paths, some outside APM. Teams need APM to (a) state its scope clearly and (b) provide stronger, verifiable integrity for everything it does install.

## Scope (children)
- [ ] #1776 - Clarify what apm-policy.yml governs (docs + positioning)
- [ ] #1778 - Make integrity guarantees legible in apm-policy.yml (two enforceable keys)
- [ ] #1777 - Deepen install-time integrity: SBOM/inventory, provenance, (deferred) signatures
- [ ] #1775 - Surface unmanaged artifacts in apm audit (drift visibility)

## Validated build sequence
Capability ships before the docs that describe it; declarable policy ships only with enforcement behind it.
- Ship 0 (now, docs-only): #1776 scoped to behavior that exists today.
- Prerequisite (gates #1778): fix `policy/inheritance.py::merge_policies`, which silently drops existing `ApmPolicy` fields (`fetch_failure`, `registry_source`, `bin_deploy`) on inheritance, and add a structural guard test so no future policy field can be dropped.
- Wave A: #1775 (extend the existing unmanaged check; add an exclude list) and #1778 (two enforceable keys: `security.integrity.require_hashes`, `security.audit.fail_on_drift`).
- Wave B: a one-line #1776 follow-up once #1775 ships; #1777 SBOM/inventory export and provenance schema.
- Deferred: #1777 signature verification, until a signing ecosystem for agent primitives exists and there is concrete demand.

## Out of scope
Runtime permission enforcement, sandboxing, or controlling what a running agent may do once installed. Those are owned by the agent harness. APM acts only at install and configuration time. Building or operating signing infrastructure is out of scope; APM consumes standard signatures where present.

## Definition of done
All four child issues closed; docs and policy consistently describe APM as the install-and-integrity layer; new integrity capabilities shipped with tests and CHANGELOG entries; every declarable policy key is backed by enforcement at the time it ships.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-15
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-15
**APM Version**: 0.20.0 (43a00c2)
**Commands Inspected**: 56 (all top-level commands and their subcommands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 4 |
| Low | 3 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### 1. `apm update --target` omits `kiro` from the listed valid values

- **Command**: `apm update --target`
- **Problem**: The `--target` flag help text lists only `claude, copilot, cursor, windsurf, codex, opencode, gemini`, but `kiro` is a supported target used by other commands (`apm install`, `apm compile`). The documentation at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/update.md` correctly includes `kiro`. This is a documentation drift between the CLI help and the reference docs.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm update --help
    -t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for (e.g. claude,
                         copilot, cursor, windsurf, codex, opencode,
                         gemini). Comma-separated for multiple: ...
  ```
  vs `apm install --help` (which is complete):
  ```
  Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all.
  ```
  vs docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/update.md`, line 46):
  ```
  Accepts a single value (claude, copilot, cursor, windsurf, kiro, codex, opencode, gemini)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--target` help text for `apm update` to list all valid values including `kiro` and `agent-skills`, matching the format used by `apm install` and `apm compile`.

---

#### 2. `apm deps update --target` omits `kiro` from both the value list and the `all` expansion

- **Command**: `apm deps update --target`
- **Problem**: The `--target` help text does not include `kiro` in its list of valid targets, and the `all` expansion is described as `copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf` (7 targets), while `apm install --target all` expands to `copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf+kiro` (8 targets). The `kiro` target is fully supported by the install pipeline.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps update --help
    -t, --target TARGET  Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                         copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                         gemini, windsurf, agent-skills, all. ...
                         'all' = copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf
                         (excludes agent-skills)
  ```
  vs `apm install --help`:
  ```
  'all' = copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf+kiro
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `kiro` to the list of accepted values in the `--target` flag description for `apm deps update`, and update the `all` expansion description to include `kiro`.

---

#### 3. Stale deprecation deadline in `apm init --plugin` runtime warning

- **Command**: `apm init --plugin`
- **Problem**: When invoked at runtime, `apm init --plugin` prints a deprecation warning saying the flag "will be removed in v0.16". The current CLI version is 0.20.0, meaning the removal deadline has already passed by four releases. This confuses users who see a flag still present well past its stated removal date.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm init --plugin
  [!] 'apm init --plugin' is deprecated. Run: apm plugin init
      Legacy flag will be removed in v0.16.
  ```
  Current version:
  ```
  $ apm --version
  Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.20.0 (43a00c2)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either remove the flag (it is past the stated deadline), or update the warning to a version-neutral statement such as "This flag will be removed in a future release."

---

#### 4. `apm cache clean` has two flags with identical descriptions performing the same action

- **Command**: `apm cache clean`
- **Problem**: The command exposes both `-f/--force` and `-y/--yes`, both documented identically as "Skip confirmation prompt". This is confusing for two reasons: (1) having two flags with the exact same help text and behavior is redundant, and (2) `--force` is used throughout the APM CLI to mean "overwrite locally-authored files on collision" (see `apm install --force`, `apm update --force`), which is a different semantic from "skip confirmation prompt". Using `--force` to skip a prompt is inconsistent with its meaning elsewhere.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm cache clean --help
  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
  ```
  Compare with `apm install --force`:
  ```
  --force  Overwrite locally-authored files on collision and deploy despite
           critical security findings
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove `-f/--force` from `apm cache clean` and keep only `-y/--yes` for confirmation skipping, consistent with `apm deps clean --yes` and `apm update --yes`. This aligns `--force` semantics across the CLI.

---

### Low Severity

#### 5. `apm mcp install --help` displays options in non-standard format

- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: Unlike all other APM subcommands, `apm mcp install` does not list its accepted options in the standard Click `Options:` block. Instead, it appends a freeform "Common options" paragraph at the bottom of the help text without proper flag formatting. Users cannot discover available flags without reading `apm install --help` separately.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Format the forwarded options as proper help entries with consistent spacing, or list the most-used forwarded options using standard Click option declarations. The freeform paragraph is hard to read and breaks the consistent `--option  Description` format users expect from all other commands.

---

#### 6. `--verbose` flag description wording is inconsistent across commands

- **Command**: Multiple commands
- **Problem**: The `-v/--verbose` flag description varies in phrasing. While some variation is appropriate, the descriptions show inconsistent style across commands.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  apm init:         Show detailed output
  apm install:      Show detailed installation information
  apm update:       Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics
  apm uninstall:    Show detailed removal information
  apm audit:        Show all findings including harmless ones
  apm mcp search:   Show detailed output
  apm run:          Show detailed output
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Adopt a consistent short template for commands where verbose simply increases output detail (e.g., "Show detailed output"), and reserve longer descriptions only where verbose genuinely changes the output semantics.

---

#### 7. `apm targets --help` usage line implies a required subcommand but the command is self-executing

- **Command**: `apm targets`
- **Problem**: The help usage line reads `Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`, which suggests a subcommand is expected (standard Click group pattern). However, `apm targets` runs successfully without a subcommand and displays the target resolution table. Users may assume a subcommand is required.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm targets --help
  Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

    Show resolved targets for the current project...
  ```
  Yet `apm targets` (no subcommand) runs and prints the table correctly.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either convert `apm targets` from a Click group to a regular command (since it has no active subcommands), or clarify in the help text that `apm targets` can be invoked directly without a subcommand.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- **`apm init`** -- deprecation warnings for `--plugin` and `--marketplace` present in help text; target flag documented correctly
- **`apm install`** -- extensive flag set documented accurately; all targets including `kiro` and `agent-skills` listed; clear error messages
- **`apm uninstall`** -- clean and concise
- **`apm compile`** -- all targets including `kiro` listed; flags documented accurately
- **`apm run`** / **`apm preview`** -- consistent flags and descriptions
- **`apm deps list/tree/info/why/clean`** -- subcommand table in docs matches CLI
- **`apm mcp list/search/show`** -- help text accurate and consistent
- **`apm config / get / set`** -- well-documented; bare `apm config` invocation shows table as documented
- **`apm runtime setup/list/status/remove`** -- flags accurate
- **`apm cache info/prune`** -- clean
- **`apm audit`** -- extensive flag set documented accurately
- **`apm doctor`** -- concise and accurate
- **`apm experimental enable/disable/list/reset`** -- consistent across subcommands
- **`apm find`**, **`apm lock`**, **`apm outdated`**, **`apm pack`**, **`apm prune`**, **`apm publish`**, **`apm search`**, **`apm self-update`**, **`apm unpack`**, **`apm view`** -- all clean
- **Error handling** -- all tested invalid invocations produce clean error messages (no stack traces):
  - `apm install --nonexistent-flag` -> "No such option" + usage hint
  - `apm deps info` (missing PACKAGE) -> "Missing argument 'PACKAGE'" + usage hint
  - `apm config set` (missing KEY) -> "Missing argument 'KEY'" + usage hint
  - `apm config list` -> "No such command 'list'" + usage hint

issues.title: [FEATURE] Move PyPI package ownership to Microsoft organization
issues.body:
The `apm-cli` package on PyPI is currently published under Daniel Meppiel's personal account. As this project is an official Microsoft tool, the package should be transferred to a Microsoft-owned PyPI organization to reflect that stewardship, improve discoverability, and provide organizational continuity independent of any individual contributor.

## Motivation

- **Organizational ownership**: Users and enterprises evaluating the tool expect Microsoft-hosted projects to be published under a verified Microsoft identity, not a personal account.
- **Continuity**: If the current publisher's account access changes, the ability to publish releases could be interrupted. Org-level ownership distributes that responsibility.
- **Trust signal**: A PyPI org namespace (e.g. under the microsoft organization) provides a stronger provenance signal for security-conscious users and automated dependency auditing tools.

## Proposed change

1. Create or use the existing `microsoft` PyPI organization (https://pypi.org/org/microsoft/).
2. Transfer ownership of `apm-cli` to that organization, or republish under a canonical Microsoft-owned name if a transfer is not feasible.
3. Update `pyproject.toml` `authors/maintainers` to reflect the org.
4. Update install documentation and any links pointing to the current PyPI page.

## References
[PyPI organization accounts documentation](https://docs.pypi.org/organization-accounts/)
Current package: https://pypi.org/project/apm-cli/

issues.title: [BUG] `apm install -g` ignores `CODEX_HOME` and always writes to `~/.codex/config.toml`
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When `apm install -g` writes Codex CLI configuration (for MCP dependencies declared in the user-scope `apm.yml`), apm hard-codes the destination to `~/.codex/config.toml` and does not consult the `CODEX_HOME` environment variable that the official Codex CLI honors.

As a result, a user who has relocated their config directory via `CODEX_HOME` (e.g. `CODEX_HOME=~/.config/codex`) still gets writes landing in `~/.codex/config.toml`. The change therefore never reaches the config that Codex actually reads (`$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`).

This concerns the user-scope (`-g`) write path; project-scope writes to `.codex/config.toml` are a separate matter.

Relevant locations (v0.20.0):

- [`CodexClientAdapter._get_codex_dir()`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.20.0/src/apm_cli/adapters/client/codex.py#L51-L56) returns a hard-coded `Path.home() / ".codex"` for the user scope and never references `CODEX_HOME`.
- The [documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.20.0/docs/src/content/docs/consumer/install-mcp-servers.md#L90) also states the destination as `~/.codex/config.toml` and does not mention `CODEX_HOME`.
- The [runtime setup script](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.20.0/scripts/runtime/setup-codex.sh#L83) also hard-codes `codex_config_dir="$HOME/.codex"`.

`CODEX_HOME` has zero references anywhere in the apm repository (code and docs).

For reference, the official Codex CLI overrides its config directory via `CODEX_HOME`, falling back to `~/.codex` only when unset. From the doc comment of [`find_codex_home()` in openai/codex](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/07298a948cbac94c7b0b505e91279fc69786f78c/codex-rs/utils/home-dir/src/lib.rs#L5-L18):

> Returns the path to the Codex configuration directory, which can be specified by the `CODEX_HOME` environment variable. If not set, defaults to `~/.codex`.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Set `CODEX_HOME` to a non-default location, e.g. `export CODEX_HOME=~/.config/codex`
2. Declare an MCP dependency in a user-scope `apm.yml`
3. Run `apm install -g`
4. Observe that the Codex config is written to `~/.codex/config.toml` instead of `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`

**Expected behavior**

`apm install -g` should resolve the Codex config directory from `CODEX_HOME` when it is set, writing to `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`, and fall back to `~/.codex/config.toml` only when `CODEX_HOME` is unset, matching the official Codex CLI behavior.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: macOS 27.0
- Python Version: 3.14.6
- APM Version: 0.20.0 (43a00c2)

**Logs**

N/A

**Additional context**

Originally raised in [discussion #1838](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/discussions/1838), where a maintainer confirmed the behavior is unintended and asked for an issue. I can send a PR that honors `CODEX_HOME`.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-22
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-22
**APM Version**: 0.21.0 (a9a883b)
**Commands Inspected**: 74

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 2     |
| Medium   | 6     |
| Low      | 3     |
| **Total**| **11**|

---

### High Severity

#### `deny` command has no CLI reference documentation page

- **Command**: `apm deny`
- **Problem**: `apm deny` is a fully implemented command (`apm deny --help` works, it revokes executable approval), but `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` has no `deny.md` page. Every other top-level command has a corresponding reference page.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deny --help
  Usage: apm deny [OPTIONS] PACKAGES...

    Revoke executable approval for packages.

    Removes entries from the ``allowExecutables`` block in ``apm.yml``.

    Example:

        apm deny owner/repo

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` contains no `deny.md`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Create `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deny.md` covering synopsis, description, options, examples, and relationship to `apm approve`.

---

#### `doctor` command has no CLI reference documentation page

- **Command**: `apm doctor`
- **Problem**: `apm doctor` is a fully implemented diagnostic command, but `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` has no `doctor.md` page. It is also absent from the reference index command table.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm doctor --help
  Usage: apm doctor [OPTIONS]

    Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI, marketplace
    config). Reports a pass/fail table and exits non-zero if a critical check
    fails.

  Options:
    -v, --verbose  Show detailed output
    --help         Show this message and exit.
  ```
  `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` contains no `doctor.md`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Create `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` covering what diagnostics are run, exit codes, and usage in CI/onboarding flows.

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm cache clean`: `--force` and `--yes` have identical descriptions

- **Command**: `apm cache clean`
- **Problem**: Two distinct flags (`-f/--force` and `-y/--yes`) share the exact same description: "Skip confirmation prompt". `--force` conventionally means "overwrite/ignore collision" (as it does in `apm install`, `apm update`, `apm pack`). Having it mean "skip confirmation" here is semantically inconsistent with every other use of `--force` in the CLI and may confuse users.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm cache clean --help
  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
    --help       Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Contrast with `apm install --force`: "Overwrite locally-authored files on collision".
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove `-f/--force` from `apm cache clean` (or change its description to match `--yes`). Standardize on `-y/--yes` for "skip confirmation" across all commands.

---

#### `apm install --runtime` help text is stale: lists `vscode` but not `--target`-compatible values

- **Command**: `apm install --runtime`
- **Problem**: `--runtime` is a legacy alias for `--target`, but its help text lists `vscode` as a valid value while `--target` does not list `vscode`. Additionally, `--runtime` omits `agent-skills` and `all` which `--target` supports. This creates confusion about what values each flag accepts.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm install --help
  --runtime TEXT    Target specific runtime only (copilot, claude, codex,
                    cursor, gemini, antigravity, intellij, kiro, opencode,
                    vscode, windsurf)
  
  -t, --target TARGET   ...Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                    gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, intellij, agent-
                    skills, all...
  ```
  `vscode` appears in `--runtime` but not `--target`. `agent-skills` and `all` appear in `--target` but not `--runtime`.
  The `compile.md` docs note: "`vscode` and `agents` are accepted as deprecated aliases for `copilot`".
- **Suggested Fix**: Update `--runtime` help text to note it is a deprecated legacy alias for `--target` and either list the same values as `--target` (noting deprecated aliases) or simply redirect users to `--target`.

---

#### `apm install --runtime` has no deprecation notice in help text

- **Command**: `apm install --runtime`
- **Problem**: The CLI reference docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md`) describe `--runtime` as "Legacy alias for `--target` (single value only). Still accepted; prefer `--target`." However, the CLI help text contains no deprecation marker, so users do not see any indication that the flag is legacy.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # CLI help shows no deprecation notice:
  --runtime TEXT    Target specific runtime only (copilot, claude, codex, ...)
  
  # Docs say (install.md):
  "--runtime VALUE | Legacy alias for `--target` (single value only). Still accepted;
   prefer `--target`."
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add "(deprecated: use --target)" to the `--runtime` help string, consistent with how `apm install --update` is annotated: "deprecated: prefer 'apm update'...".

---

#### `apm compile --no-dedup` / `--no-force-instructions` double-negative flag naming

- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: The flag is displayed as `--no-dedup / --no-force-instructions`. The description says "Include the instructions section in CLAUDE.md..." (the positive action), but the primary flag name `--no-dedup` uses a "no" prefix meaning "disable deduplication = include instructions". The complementary flag `--no-force-instructions` is also prefixed with "no". Both options in the pair use "no", making it hard to remember which enables the behavior.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm compile --help
    --no-dedup / --no-force-instructions
                          Include the instructions section in CLAUDE.md even
                          when .claude/rules/ is already populated. Overrides
                          the default deduplication...
                          Alias: --force-instructions.
  ```
  Users must mentally parse "no-dedup = force include instructions" vs "no-force-instructions = keep dedup (default)". The alias `--force-instructions` is clearer but is only mentioned at the end of the description.
- **Suggested Fix**: Rename the primary flag to `--force-instructions` (the alias is already clearer), making the pair `--force-instructions / --no-force-instructions`. Drop `--no-dedup` as the primary name (keep as an alias if backward compatibility is needed).

---

#### Reference index command table is missing 8 commands

- **Command**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md`
- **Problem**: The phase-based command reference table omits 8 commands that exist in the CLI and each have their own docs pages.
- **Evidence**:
  The table in `reference/index.md` covers: `init`, `install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `view`, `deps`, `outdated`, `list`, `audit`, `compile`, `prune`, `targets`, `runtime`, `cache`, `config`, `run`, `pack`, `unpack`, `preview`, `marketplace`, `search`, `policy`, `mcp`, `experimental`.

  Missing from the table (but present in CLI and with docs pages):
  - `approve` (`approve.md` exists)
  - `deny` (no docs page -- separate issue above)
  - `doctor` (no docs page -- separate issue above)
  - `find` (`find.md` exists)
  - `lock` (`lock.md` exists)
  - `plugin` (`plugin.md` exists)
  - `publish` (`publish.md` exists)
  - `self-update` (`self-update.md` exists)
- **Suggested Fix**: Add all 8 missing commands to the reference index table under appropriate phases (e.g., `approve`/`deny` under Governance; `doctor`/`self-update` under a new "Maintenance" phase; `find`/`lock` under Inspect and audit; `plugin`/`publish` under Author and distribute).

---

#### `apm config --help` does not mention the no-subcommand config display behavior

- **Command**: `apm config`
- **Problem**: Running `apm config` with no subcommand displays a useful merged project+global configuration table. This behavior is documented in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/config.md` but is completely absent from the CLI `--help` text. Users relying only on `--help` will not discover it.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config --help
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

    Configure APM CLI

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

  Commands:
    get    Get a configuration value
    set    Set a configuration value
    unset  Unset a configuration value
  ```
  No mention of bare `apm config` showing the table. Contrast with actual behavior:
  ```
  $ apm config
  Current APM Configuration
  +----------+------------------+--------------------------+
  | Category | Setting          | Value                    |
  +----------+------------------+--------------------------+
  | Project  | Name             | apm                      |
  | ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a note to the `apm config` group description, e.g.: "With no subcommand, prints the merged project + global configuration table."

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm mcp list` and `apm mcp search` have inconsistent `--limit` defaults

- **Commands**: `apm mcp list`, `apm mcp search`
- **Problem**: Both commands expose a `--limit` flag for the same conceptual purpose (cap the number of results), but default to different values: `list` defaults to 20, `search` defaults to 10.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp list --help
    --limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 20]

  $ apm mcp search --help
    --limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 10]
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Align both to the same default (20 seems reasonable for both). The docs (`mcp.md`) correctly reflect the current values, so update whichever command is changed.

---

#### `apm targets --help` shows `COMMAND [ARGS]...` in usage with no listed subcommands

- **Command**: `apm targets`
- **Problem**: The usage line reads `apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...` suggesting subcommands exist, but no `Commands:` section appears in the help. CLI-only users have no way to discover this is intentional (future subcommands are reserved). The `targets.md` docs explain it clearly, but the help text does not.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm targets --help
  Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

    Show resolved targets for the current project...

  Options:
    --json  Output as JSON instead of a table.
    --all   Include the agent-skills meta-target in JSON output...
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  No `Commands:` section shown. The `targets.md` docs note: "no subcommands ship today... reserved for future use."
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a note to the help text such as "(subcommands reserved for future use)" or restructure `apm targets` as a plain command (not a group) until subcommands are implemented.

---

#### `apm deps update` is listed in `apm deps --help` without a visible deprecation marker

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: `apm deps update` is deprecated in favor of `apm update`, which the docs note prominently. However, the `apm deps --help` output lists `update` with the plain description "Update APM dependencies to latest refs" -- no deprecation signal. Users must run `apm deps update --help` to see the deprecation caution block in the detailed docs.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps --help
  Commands:
    clean   Remove all APM dependencies
    info    Show detailed package information
    list    List installed APM dependencies
    tree    Show dependency tree structure
    update  Update APM dependencies to latest refs   <-- no deprecated marker
    why     Explain why a package is installed...
  ```
  Compare with `apm install --update`: "Update dependencies to latest Git references (deprecated: prefer 'apm update'...)" -- which clearly labels the deprecation inline.
- **Suggested Fix**: Prefix the `apm deps update` description with "(deprecated: use 'apm update' instead)" to match the inline deprecation pattern used by `apm install --update`.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands/areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- **`apm init`** -- clear help, consistent `-v/--verbose`, `-y/--yes` flags
- **`apm install`** (core behavior) -- comprehensive flag documentation, good error messages for missing args
- **`apm uninstall`** -- consistent flags, sensible error handling
- **`apm update`** -- consistent deprecation labeling of `--update`  
- **`apm compile`** (except `--no-dedup`) -- thorough option docs
- **`apm run` / `apm preview`** -- symmetric, consistent flag set
- **`apm deps list/tree/info/clean/why`** -- clear descriptions, correct required-arg error messages
- **`apm mcp search/show/install`** -- well-documented, consistent verbose flag
- **`apm config get/set/unset`** -- correct behavior, good validation error messages
- **`apm runtime setup/list/remove/status`** -- consistent, complete help
- **`apm audit`** -- exceptionally thorough flag documentation
- **`apm cache info/prune`** -- clean, minimal, clear
- **`apm marketplace`** (all subcommands) -- comprehensive and consistent
- **`apm experimental`** (all subcommands) -- clear flag behavior, good JSON flag
- **`apm lock / apm lock export`** -- dual command/group pattern works well
- **`apm approve`** -- clear with good examples in help
- **`apm outdated`** -- concise and correct
- **`apm pack`** -- very detailed, good exit code documentation
- **`apm publish`** -- clear experimental gating
- **`apm search`** -- minimal and correct
- **`apm self-update`** -- clear check-only mode
- **`apm find`** -- good exit code behavior
- **`apm list`** -- simple, correct
- **`apm plugin init`** -- consistent with `apm init`
- **`apm policy status`** -- thorough output format options
- **`apm prune`** -- consistent `--dry-run` usage
- **`apm view`** -- clear field documentation
- **`apm unpack`** -- clear deprecation notice inline
- **Error handling** -- All tested commands (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info`, `apm config set`, `apm mcp show`) produce clean "Missing argument" / "No such option" messages with usage hints. No stack traces observed.

issues.title: [BUG] hook_integrator merges all per-harness hook manifests into every target (codex/cursor hooks leak into .claude/settings.json)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator` does not select a single per-harness hook manifest when integrating a package's hooks. Instead, for a package that ships multiple per-harness hook manifests (`hooks.json`, `hooks-codex.json`, `hooks-cursor.json`), it merges **all** of them into **every** target, irrespective of which harness each manifest is meant for and irrespective of which targets are enabled.

The result is that a single target's hook config (e.g. `.claude/settings.json`) ends up containing:

- the foreign Codex hook command (`session-start-codex`), which is wrong for Claude, and
- the Cursor manifest's lower-case `sessionStart` event with a relative `./hooks/run-hook.cmd` path, which is invalid for both Claude and Codex.

Three distinct defects are visible in one reproduction (all in `hook_integrator`):

1. **No per-target manifest selection (primary).** `hooks-codex.json` and `hooks-cursor.json` are integrated into the `claude` target, and `hooks.json` + `hooks-cursor.json` into the `codex` target. The filename suffix that identifies the harness (`-codex`, `-cursor`) is ignored.
2. **Each manifest is processed twice.** The integrator walks both `<pkg>/hooks/` and `<pkg>/.apm/hooks/`, so every manifest is integrated from two source dirs (`12 hook(s) integrated (6 adopted)` = 3 manifests × 2 dirs × 2 targets).
3. **Hook-script path is doubled during validation.** The "script exists" check resolves `.../superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd` as `.../superpowers/hooks/hooks/run-hook.cmd` (extra `hooks/` segment) and emits a spurious `Hook script not found` warning, even though the deployed command (`.claude/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd`) is correct and present.

The lower-case `sessionStart` from the Cursor manifest also triggers a `hook event casing mismatch` warning against **both** the `claude` and `codex` targets, because the Cursor manifest is fed into integrators that expect PascalCase.

**To Reproduce**

`obra/superpowers` is a convenient public repro: it ships three per-harness hook manifests under both `hooks/` and `.apm/hooks/`:

| manifest | intended harness | event key | command |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hooks.json` | claude | `SessionStart` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/run-hook.cmd session-start` |
| `hooks-codex.json` | codex | `SessionStart` | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/run-hook.cmd session-start-codex` |
| `hooks-cursor.json` | cursor | `sessionStart` | `./hooks/run-hook.cmd session-start` |

Steps:

1. In an empty git repo:
   ```
   apm install obra/superpowers --target claude,codex
   ```
2. Inspect `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json`.

(It also reproduces with a single target, e.g. `--target claude`, and with `--skill <name>` selection — neither narrows the hooks.)

**Expected behavior**

- The `claude` target should integrate **only** `hooks.json`.
- The `codex` target should integrate **only** `hooks-codex.json`.
- `hooks-cursor.json` should be integrated only when `cursor` is a target.
- `.claude/settings.json` should contain a single `SessionStart` entry pointing at `session-start`; no `session-start-codex`, no lower-case `sessionStart`.
- No `casing mismatch` warning for `claude`/`codex` (the lower-case event belongs to the Cursor manifest only).
- No `Hook script not found` warning for a script that exists.

**Actual behavior**

`apm install obra/superpowers --target claude,codex` produces a contaminated `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "matcher": "startup|resume|clear",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "\".claude/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd\" session-start-codex", "async": false }
        ]
      },
      {
        "matcher": "startup|clear|compact",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "\".claude/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd\" session-start", "async": false }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "sessionStart": [
      { "command": "./hooks/run-hook.cmd session-start" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The first `SessionStart` entry runs the **Codex** hook script inside Claude, and the trailing lower-case `sessionStart` is the **Cursor** manifest. `.codex/hooks.json` is symmetric: it carries the Claude `session-start` (which relies on `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, undefined under Codex) plus the same lower-case `sessionStart`.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)
- Python Version: n/a — installed via the standalone CLI binary (PyInstaller bundle, `apm_cli` 0.21.0), not a venv
- APM Version: 0.21.0 (975f8f0)
- VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a
- Harnesses / targets: `claude`, `codex`
- Affected package: `obra/superpowers` (commit `896224c4` at time of repro)

**Logs**

Relevant lines from `apm install obra/superpowers --target claude,codex` (with `APM_LOG_LEVEL=INFO`):

```
INFO apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator target claude: detected hook event: SessionStart
Hook script not found: .../apm_modules/obra/superpowers/.apm/hooks/hooks/run-hook.cmd
INFO apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator target claude: detected hook event: sessionStart
Hook events for target 'claude' may not be recognized: sessionStart. Target expects PascalCase (e.g. PreToolUse). Rename events to match the PascalCase convention, then reinstall.
WARNING apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator target claude: hook event casing mismatch (no mapping): sessionStart
...
Hook script not found: .../apm_modules/obra/superpowers/hooks/hooks/run-hook.cmd
...
WARNING apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator target codex: hook event casing mismatch (no mapping): sessionStart
  |-- 12 hook(s) integrated (6 adopted) -> .claude/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json
  |   SessionStart: runs .claude/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks-codex.json)
  |   sessionStart: runs ./hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks-cursor.json)
  |   SessionStart: runs .claude/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks.json)
  |   SessionStart: runs .codex/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks-codex.json)
  |   sessionStart: runs ./hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks-cursor.json)
  |   SessionStart: runs .codex/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks.json)
```

The integration summary itself shows all three manifests being applied to both targets.

**Additional context**

- No per-package knob works around this: `--target <single>` still merges the foreign manifests, and `--skill` only filters skills, not hooks. There appears to be no `--no-hooks` / hook-exclude option.
- Likely fix area: when integrating hooks for target `T`, select the manifest whose harness suffix matches `T` (`hooks.json` → claude default, `hooks-<harness>.json` → that harness), and don't fan a manifest out to non-matching targets. Also dedupe the `hooks/` vs `.apm/hooks/` source dirs, and fix the doubled `hooks/hooks/` path in the script-existence check.
- Possibly related (hook integration): #1823 ("Cursor hook integration omits required top-level `version` in `.cursor/hooks.json`").

issues.title: apm install --update silently skips packages when both repo URL and tag change simultaneously
issues.body:
## Bug Report

### Summary

When a package in `apm.yml` is updated to point to a **new repository** _and_ a **new tag** simultaneously (e.g. after a monorepo reorganisation), `apm install --update` reports _"No changes — install state already up to date"_ and does **not** update the lock file or the installed files. The stale lock entry is silently carried forward.

### APM version

```
Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.21.0 (975f8f0)
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a package installed at an old location, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   # apm.yml (before)
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - private-org/old-repo/content/my-package#my-package/v1.0.0
   ```
   Lock file contains:
   ```yaml
   - repo_url: private-org/old-repo
     resolved_ref: my-package/v1.0.0
     virtual_path: content/my-package
   ```

2. Update `apm.yml` to point to the package's new canonical location (same package name, new repo + new path):
   ```yaml
   # apm.yml (after)
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - private-org/new-repo/packages/category/subcategory/my-package#my-package/v1.1.0
   ```

3. Run:
   ```
   apm install --update --target copilot
   ```

### Actual behaviour

```
[i] No changes -- install state already up to date in 0.2s.
```

Lock file is **not** updated. Still contains the old `repo_url`, `resolved_ref`, and `virtual_path`.

### Expected behaviour

APM should detect that the declared dependency in `apm.yml` no longer matches the locked entry (different `repo_url` + different tag), re-resolve, update the lock, and install the new version.

### Verbose output (smoking gun)

```
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
Parsed apm.yml: 1 APM deps, 0 MCP deps
Loaded apm.lock.yaml for SHA comparison (2 dependencies)
    private-org/old-repo/sdlc/agents: locked at 673c47f8
Resolved 1 direct dependencies (no transitive)
...
apm.lock.yaml unchanged -- skipping write
[i] No changes -- install state already up to date in 0.2s.
```

`apm.yml` contains **12** APM dependency entries, but `Parsed apm.yml: 1 APM deps` — only 1 is being processed for resolution. The resolver appears to skip packages already present in the lock file by matching on package name / tag stem, without validating that `repo_url` or `virtual_path` still match the declaration in `apm.yml`.

### Lock file drift (before vs after)

| Field | apm.yml (declared) | apm.lock.yaml (stale) |
|---|---|---|
| repo | `private-org/new-repo` | `private-org/old-repo` |
| tag | `my-package/v1.1.0` | `my-package/v1.0.0` |
| virtual_path | `packages/category/subcategory/my-package` | `content/my-package` |

Same pattern observed for two other packages migrated in the same operation.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | macOS Darwin |
| APM version | 0.21.0 (975f8f0) |
| Lock file `apm_version` | 0.18.0 (generated 2026-06-15, before the edit) |
| Command | `apm install --update --target copilot` (run from `~`) |
| Cache | 8 git repos, 10 checkouts, 274.7 MB |

`apm.yml` (illustrative — all refs anonymised):
```yaml
name: global
version: 1.0.0
dependencies:
  apm:
  - private-org/old-repo/devops/pkg-a#pkg-a/v1.0.0
  - private-org/old-repo/architecture/pkg-b#pkg-b/v1.1.0
  - private-org/new-repo/packages/category/subcategory/my-package#my-package/v1.1.0
  - private-org/new-repo/packages/category/subcategory/pkg-c#pkg-c/v0.2.0
  - private-org/new-repo/packages/category/subcategory/pkg-d#pkg-d/v1.0.0
  - private-org/toolkit-repo/packages/toolkit#toolkit/v0.5.1
  - public-author/public-package
  - /local/path/to/package  # local dep
  mcp: []
```

### Workaround

Manually edit `apm.lock.yaml` to remove the stale entries, then re-run `apm install`. APM will re-resolve and install correctly.

Alternatively, `apm cache clean` followed by `apm install` also forces a full re-resolution.

### Impact

This affects any user who **migrates a package from one repository to another** (e.g. monorepo reorg, marketplace consolidation) while keeping the same package name/tag stem. The silent no-op is particularly dangerous because there is no warning — the user assumes the update succeeded.

### Hypothesis

The resolver's drift-detection logic appears to match lock entries by **tag stem** (e.g. `my-package`) rather than by the full `(repo_url, resolved_ref, virtual_path)` tuple. When the tag name is unchanged (same package name, version bumped OR same version in a new repo), the lock entry is considered a match and the re-resolution is skipped.
